generated_test_cases.title: Retrieve database session successfully
generated_test_cases.description: Test that get_db returns a valid database session when called during normal operation.
steps: Call get_db function to obtain a database session
Use the session to execute a simple query such as SELECT 1
expected_results: get_db returns a non-null session object
The query returns the expected result (e.g., 1)

generated_test_cases.title: Database session closed after use
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that the database session is properly closed after the context exits.
steps: Call get_db and store the session
Close the session explicitly using session.close()
Attempt to execute a query with the closed session
expected_results: Closing the session does not raise an exception
Executing a query with a closed session raises an exception indicating the session is closed

generated_test_cases.title: Handle database connection failure
generated_test_cases.description: Ensure that get_db handles a connection failure gracefully and reports an error.
steps: Simulate a database connection failure (e.g., by providing an invalid connection URL)
expected_results: get_db raises an appropriate exception (e.g., sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError)

generated_test_cases.title: Prevent SQL injection via get_db
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that get_db does not expose vulnerabilities to SQL injection through session creation.
steps: Attempt to inject malicious input into any parameter used in get_db (none in this case)
expected_results: get_db executes without interpreting injected payload as SQL

generated_test_cases.title: Integration test with actual database
generated_test_cases.description: Test get_db integration with a real database by creating, querying, and cleaning up a test record.
steps: Call get_db to obtain a session
Insert a test record into the database
Query the record to verify insertion
expected_results: All database operations succeed without errors
The test record is correctly inserted, retrieved, and deleted

steps: Invoke dependency_error with an empty dependency list
expected_results: Function should handle gracefully, possibly returning True or no operation

generated_test_cases.title: Security: Dependency Injection Attack

expected_results: The function should sanitize input and reject the malicious dependency

generated_test_cases.title: Exception Handling: Unexpected Exception During Dependency Check

expected_results: The function should catch the exception and return an appropriate error status or rethrow

generated_test_cases.title: Create Job - Successful

expected_results: Response status code is 201.
Response body matches the JobOut schema with the same 'name' and a generated 'id'.

generated_test_cases.title: Create Job - Missing Name
generated_test_cases.description: Attempt to create a job without providing the required 'name' field to trigger validation error.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/jobs/ with an empty JSON object.
expected_results: Response status code is 422 (Unprocessable Entity).
Response body contains validation error indicating 'name' field is required.

Send a PUT request to /api/jobs/123 with valid update data.
expected_results: Response status code is 409 (Conflict) or appropriate error defined by the dependency check.

generated_test_cases.title: Update Job - Successful
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that updating an existing job with valid data returns 200 and updated job details.
steps: Send a PUT request to /api/jobs/123 with a JSON body containing a new 'name' value.
expected_results: Response status code is 200.
Response body matches the JobOut schema with the updated 'name' and unchanged 'id' and 'state'.
